It operates by comparing local HEAD pointers against the canonical 'main' reference via git's internal directed acyclic graph (DAG) structure. The mergeability feasibility indicator M extends this by incorporating external metadata from the GitHub API, enabling automated triage of orphaned branches. Both primitives rely on the assumption that version control systems provide idempotent, collision-resistant hashes; however, in practice, rebase operations can rewrite history, causing false positives in the ahead-count calculation. To mitigate this, we introduce a robustness threshold \theta such that only branches with AheadCount > \theta trigger active review. This threshold balances developer autonomy against resource consumption, preventing an explosion of low-value technical-debt tickets while ensuring critical integrations proceed smoothly.
